questions.question: Shadow Root is best described as:

options.text: A document fragment that is the root of a shadow tree attached to a host

questions.explanation: The shadow root is the root node of the shadow tree; it's attached to the host element and encapsulates content/styles.

questions.question: What is the 'light DOM'?

options.text: The DOM nodes authored by the page author that get slotted into a component

questions.explanation: Light DOM = the regular DOM children you write in markup; they're projected into the shadow tree via <slot>.

questions.question: How do you style light-DOM children from INSIDE the shadow tree?
questions.explanation: ::slotted() targets distributed light-DOM children. You can only style the slot's top-level assigned nodes, not their descendants.

questions.question: A <slot> with no content projected shows its:

options.text: Fallback content (children of the slot element)

questions.explanation: Default/fallback content placed inside <slot> renders when no matching light-DOM child is assigned.

questions.question: CSS custom properties (__var) penetrate shadow boundaries. Why is that useful?

options.text: They let a host theme a component's internals while keeping other styles encapsulated
They only work in closed mode

questions.explanation: CSS variables inherit through shadow boundaries, making them the standard way to expose theming hooks without leaking other styles.

questions.question: Attach a shadow root in JS with:
questions.explanation: attachShadow({mode:'open'|'closed'}) creates and returns the shadow root. open lets element.shadowRoot be read.

questions.question: In Angular, the DEFAULT ViewEncapsulation is:
questions.explanation: Angular defaults to Emulated encapsulation (attribute-scoped selectors) for broad browser support; ShadowDom uses real shadow roots.

questions.question: Event retargeting means a click inside a component is seen by outside listeners as targeting:

options.text: The shadow host element (not internal nodes)

questions.explanation: Retargeting preserves encapsulation: external listeners see the host as the event target, hiding internal structure.
